blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: Name it or reuse the shared DEBOUNCE_MS so the composer and the draft save stay in step.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: DRAFT_KEY is the same for every stage. After a host or agent switch, the next stage reads the previous agent’s text and can send it to the wrong agent.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Include the agent id in the draft key, so each agent keeps its own draft on each stage.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: Open a draft for coord, switch the stage to ds-rly, and check that the composer is empty.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: Sign-out clears the session but not relay.draft.* keys. On a shared device the next person can read the last draft.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Clear stored drafts when the session ends.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: Sign out with a draft open, sign back in, and check that the draft is gone.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: The spec caps reconnects at 5 tries, then shows “Hub not reachable”. Here attempt grows without a limit and each retry waits longer, so the stage never reaches the failed state.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Stop retrying after a fixed number of attempts and show the banner with a manual retry.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: Stop the hub and check that retries end after the last attempt.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: role="alert" re-announces on each attempt. The shared rule is one polite status line that changes only when the state changes.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Announce the first retry only, then announce again when the socket returns.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: With a screen reader on, drop the socket and count the announcements.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: Between attempts the banner keeps the word “Reconnecting”. The spec’s idle copy is “Waiting to reconnect”.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: web/AGENTS.md asks for a test for each new recovery path. The added tests cover save and restore, but not a socket close with unsent text.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Add a test that drops the socket while a draft is open and checks that it is restored.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: Run the unit tests and check that the new case fails without the fix.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: The behaviour change is user-visible. Add one line to the description so reviewers and release notes pick it up.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: “works” doesn’t say which path is tested. Name it after the behaviour: “restores the draft after a reconnect”.

blocks.label: Why

Why
paragraphs: role="alert" re-announces on each attempt. The shared rule is one polite status line that changes only when the state changes.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: Between attempts the banner keeps the word “Reconnecting”. The spec’s idle copy is “Waiting to reconnect”.

blocks.label: Suggested patch
blocks.patch:
- const idleCopy = "Reconnecting";
+ const idleCopy = "Waiting to reconnect";

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: web/AGENTS.md asks for a test for each new recovery path. The added tests cover save and restore, but not a socket close with unsent text.

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: The reconnect test restores coord’s draft into the ds-rly stage.
The restore path reads the stored draft without checking which agent and stage wrote it, so the composer can send it to the wrong agent after a switch.

blocks.label: Recommendation
paragraphs: Store the agent and stage with the draft and skip the restore when either differs.

blocks.label: How to verify
paragraphs: Write a draft for coord, switch to ds-rly, reconnect, and check that the composer is empty.

blocks.label: Requirement
paragraphs: A draft restores only into the agent and stage it was written for.

blocks.label: Suggested patch
blocks.patch:
-   const draft = sessionStorage.getItem(DRAFT_KEY);
+   const draft = readDraft(DRAFT_KEY, agentId, stageId);

blocks.label: Why
paragraphs: useStageSocket.ts computes 1000 * attempt; the hub socket calls backoff(attempt).
Other sockets in web/src use backoff() for their retry delay. This one multiplies by the attempt count directly.

blocks.label: Requirement
paragraphs: Retry delays use the shared backoff helper.

postSheet.title: Post 3 findings to CodeCommit
postSheet.lead: Each finding becomes a PR comment on #451, anchored to its file and line.

F1.claim: Draft key ignores the agent, so a draft can restore into another agent’s stage
F1.why: DRAFT_KEY is the same for every stage. After a host or agent switch, the next stage reads the previous agent’s text and can send it to the wrong agent.

F2.claim: Reconnect retries forever when the hub stays down
F2.why: The spec caps reconnects at 5 tries, then shows “Hub not reachable”. Here attempt grows without a limit and each retry waits longer, so the stage never reaches the failed state.

F3.claim: Drafts stay in session storage after sign-out
F3.why: Sign-out clears the session but not relay.draft.* keys. On a shared device the next person can read the last draft.

F4.claim: Retry banner announces every attempt, flooding screen readers
F4.why: role="alert" re-announces on each attempt. The shared rule is one polite status line that changes only when the state changes.

F5.claim: No test covers a reconnect while a draft is open
F5.why: web/AGENTS.md asks for a test for each new recovery path. The added tests cover save and restore, but not a socket close with unsent text.

F6.why: Name it or reuse the shared DEBOUNCE_MS so the composer and the draft save stay in step.

F7.claim: Idle copy says “Reconnecting” when nothing is retrying
F7.why: Between attempts the banner keeps the word “Reconnecting”. The spec’s idle copy is “Waiting to reconnect”.

F8.claim: Test name doesn’t say what case it covers
F8.why: “works” doesn’t say which path is tested. Name it after the behaviour: “restores the draft after a reconnect”.

F9.claim: PR description doesn’t say drafts survive an agent switch
F9.why: The behaviour change is user-visible. Add one line to the description so reviewers and release notes pick it up.

F10.claim: Fix clears the draft when the retry banner closes, before the socket is back
F10.why: The new onClose handler calls clearDraft(). Closing the banner while the socket is still reconnecting drops the text the fix was meant to keep.

F11.claim: A restored draft can be sent to a stage it wasn’t written for
F11.why: The restore path reads the stored draft without checking which agent and stage wrote it, so the composer can send it to the wrong agent after a switch.

extra.requirement: A draft restores only into the agent and stage it was written for.
extra.evidence: The reconnect test restores coord’s draft into the ds-rly stage.
extra.rec: Store the agent and stage with the draft and skip the restore when either differs.
extra.verify: Write a draft for coord, switch to ds-rly, reconnect, and check that the composer is empty.

F12.claim: Retry delay is written inline instead of using the shared backoff helper
F12.why: Other sockets in web/src use backoff() for their retry delay. This one multiplies by the attempt count directly.

extra.requirement: Retry delays use the shared backoff helper.
extra.evidence: useStageSocket.ts computes 1000 * attempt; the hub socket calls backoff(attempt).

summary.changed: Keeps the composer draft in session storage while a stage reconnects and restores it when the socket returns. Adds a retry banner and moves reconnect timing into useStageSocket.

prose: This pull request keeps what you’ve typed in the composer when a stage loses its connection. The draft is saved to session storage while the socket reconnects and is put back once the socket returns.
Reconnect timing moves out of the stage view into useStageSocket, which now owns the retry loop and the retry banner. The view only reads whether the stage is connected, retrying or unreachable.
The change touches three files: the new useDraft hook, useStageSocket, and the stage view that wires them together. There are no changes to the hub or to the message format.

chapters.title: Why drafts were lost
chapters.problem: A reconnect remounted the stage, and the composer started empty.
chapters.before: Text typed before a reconnect was gone.
chapters.after: The draft is read back from session storage on mount.
decisions: Session storage, not local storage, so drafts end with the tab.

chapters.title: Keying drafts per agent
chapters.problem: Drafts were stored under one key per stage, so two agents on the same stage overwrote each other’s text.
chapters.before: Switching from coord to ds-rly on one stage showed coord’s draft.
chapters.after: Each agent keeps its own draft on each stage.
decisions: The key is DRAFT_KEY.agentId.stageId, not a hash, so it stays readable in devtools.
Old stage-only keys are left alone; they end with the session.

chapters.title: Bounded reconnect
chapters.problem: The socket retried on every close, with no limit.
chapters.before: A hub that stayed down kept the stage retrying for good.
chapters.after: Retries back off, but there’s still no cap; the P0 finding covers it.
decisions: Backoff doubles from 1 second to 30 seconds.

chapters.title: Tests and what they prove
chapters.problem: The PR changes recovery after a reconnect, so the tests should prove a draft survives one.
chapters.before: No test opened a draft and dropped the socket.
chapters.after: The tests check the key per agent; nothing yet drops the socket with a draft open.
decisions: Unit tests only; the browser check covers the banner.

checklist.q: Tests cover the new recovery path
checklist.note: No test reconnects with a draft open (P1).

checklist.q: Drafts are kept per agent and stage
checklist.note: The key includes agentId once the P0 fix lands.

checklist.q: Reconnect stops when the hub stays down

checklist.note: Drafts are session-only, so there’s nothing to migrate.
